# IV. Trust and understanding {.unnumbered}

A product is not trustworthy merely because it published successfully once. Teams need to explain failures, understand dependencies, discover ownership, and apply organizational rules without hiding them in prose.

This part focuses on evidence around the delivery: diagnostics, lineage, metadata, policies, output ports, and service-level expectations. It also draws careful boundaries around what the current implementation can prove. Incomplete lineage is reported as incomplete. A descriptive access label is not an IAM grant. A policy check is not a substitute for organizational authorization.

::: {.callout-note title="By the end of this part"}
You should be able to diagnose a blocked run, distinguish several kinds of lineage, attach business metadata, and describe how policies, ports, and SLAs extend a product definition.
:::
